clinician.trajectory_summary: A 3-year-old boy presented with recurrent fever, painful urination, increased urinary frequency, and hematuria over one year. Initial dipstick tests suggested UTI but no definitive culture or imaging was done. Abdominal ultrasound revealed a left renal mass with cystic lesions and renal pelvis destruction with calcifications. Urine culture from resected tissue showed no bacterial growth after 7 days. Surgical resection of the affected kidney was performed, and histology showed foamy lipid-laden macrophages with chronic inflammatory cells and fibrosis, confirming xanthogranulomatous pyelophinitis. Postoperatively, the patient was treated with intravenous Tazobactam/piperacillin and discharged in good condition.
